notes.priority: PROJECT DRAWING / SPECIFICATION > PROJECT-SPECIFIC OWNER OVERRIDE > URBAN PROJECTS OWNER STANDARD > UNKNOWN / ASK OWNER
notes.a_default_never_bypasses_geometry: where a rule carries a dimension and the drawing establishes another, the drawing wins. Where the geometry a rule needs is not established, the rule's unknown_behavior applies and no default dimension is used
notes.source: Owner rule addendum, Urban Projects, 2026-09-17: stairs, open American pantry, elevator marble
notes.three_concepts: CONSTRUCTION_VOCABULARY says what a term means; MEASUREMENT_RULE says how the quantity is measured; COMMERCIAL_MEASUREMENT_BASIS says how the work is bought. A RATE — what a supplier charges, on a quotation, on a date — lives in a project rate card and never in this library
notes.source_6e_a: Owner rule addendum 6E-A, 2026-09-17: stair thicknesses, commercial step measurement, elevator threshold fallback, vocabulary
notes.qs_rule_pack_finishes_v1: received 2026-09-17. Ceramic, stairs and waterproofing, plus the general rules that govern all three
notes.qs_rule_pack_finishes_v1_status: TRUNCATED AS RECEIVED: the CERAMIC, STAIRS and WATERPROOFING sections each end in an ellipsis. What arrived is recorded; what did not is not invented, and the missing items are an OWNER_RULE_REQUEST

rules.rule_name: An American pantry is a functional zone, never forced into a closed room
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §A
required_geometry: the physical space the pantry zone sits in
rules.calculation_method: PHYSICAL_SPACE -> FUNCTIONAL_ZONE = OPEN_AMERICAN_PANTRY -> TRADE_MEASUREMENT_ZONE. The zone creates no wall and closes no edge
exceptions: a pantry the drawing shows enclosed on four sides is a CLOSED_PANTRY and an ordinary physical space
rules.notes: the openness of a particular pantry is a project-level answer: the drawing, or the owner for that project

rules.rule_name: An open edge tiles nothing
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §A
required_geometry: which sides of the zone have no wall on them
rules.calculation_method: WALL_TILE_LENGTH = 0 on an edge open toward DINING, SALOON, LIVING, RECEPTION or OPEN CIRCULATION. The zone is never closed virtually to produce a wall

rules.rule_name: An American pantry receives full-wall tile on its applicable walls
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §B
required_geometry: the host wall segments of the pantry installation
the MEP or sanitary drawing where available
rules.calculation_method: FULL_WALL tile on the actual host walls of the installation. The arrangement is ONE_WALL, L_SHAPED, U_SHAPED or OTHER_DRAWN_CONFIGURATION, derived from the geometry and never from the word PANTRY
exceptions: never tile the perimeter of an imaginary closed pantry
rules.notes: the wall serving the water, plumbing and counter arrangement is the one to identify first

rules.rule_name: Wall tile height is never assumed
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §B
required_geometry: a project, drawing or owner height rule
rules.calculation_method: the height comes from the project, the drawing or the owner. No universal height exists in this engine

rules.rule_name: Kuwait villa and chalet stairs are marble unless the project says otherwise
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §C
required_geometry: the stair assemblies of the project
rules.calculation_method: MARBLE on TREAD (نايم), RISER (قائم) and LANDING (استراحة) of EVERY stair assembly — main, secondary, service, roof, external steps — not only the main staircase
exceptions: a drawing, specification or owner statement that establishes another finish for a stair overrides this
rules.notes: the finish rule is applied to stairs the engine has DETECTED. A stair-like observation nobody reconstructed is unresolved, not marble

rules.rule_name: Stair geometry comes from the drawing, never from typical values
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §D
rules.calculation_method: each figure from the floor-to-floor height, the sections, the levels, the stair details and the CAD geometry. A 16 cm riser, a 30 cm tread and a 120 cm width are EXAMPLES and may be used diagnostically only

rules.rule_name: The visible marble riser is the step rise less the tread build-up
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §E
required_geometry: the tread marble thickness or build-up detail
rules.calculation_method: VISIBLE_RISER_HEIGHT = step_rise - tread_marble_thickness. TREAD_M2 = stair_width x tread_depth; RISER_VISIBLE_M2 = stair_width x VISIBLE_RISER_HEIGHT. The owner's worked example is 1.20 x 0.30 = 0.360 m2 of tread and 1.20 x (0.16 - 0.03) = 0.156 m2 of riser, 0.516 m2 per step — an EXAMPLE, not a constant
exceptions: 13 cm is never hardcoded: it is the example's arithmetic, not a standard

rules.rule_name: Stair units stay apart, and a measurement basis is not a pricing basis
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §F
rules.calculation_method: TREAD, RISER and LANDING are m2; NOSING, STAIR SKIRTING and RAILING PATH are lm. m2 + lm + pcs is never summed. GEOMETRIC_MEASUREMENT_UNIT and CONTRACTOR_COMMERCIAL_PRICING_BASIS are separate fields: a contractor may quote stair work on another basis while the physical marble quantity stays an area

rules.rule_name: A stair landing is marble, and is never also porcelain floor
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §G
rules.calculation_method: the landing's actual polygon in m2, with the invariant MARBLE_STAIR_AREA n PORCELAIN_FLOOR_AREA = 0 m2
exceptions: a piece of floor between the flights that is not a landing — a floor plate, a void, circulation — is not stair marble

rules.rule_name: Every elevator landing station is a separate measurable occurrence
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §H
required_geometry: the landing doors on each floor
rules.calculation_method: ELEVATOR_LANDING_MARBLE_ASSEMBLY per station: one elevator serving four floors is four stations, and two doors on one floor are two landing-door assemblies. The shaft alone is never the count
rules.notes: declared for the later trade and BOQ phase. Nothing is measured on a project until its geometry is established

rules.rule_name: Marble surrounds the outer landing door on three sides, 0.50 m by default
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §I, with the owner's reference image
rules.calculation_method: LEFT, TOP and RIGHT of the OUTER landing door, 0.50 m wide unless the drawing, detail or specification establishes another width. Measured as the AREA of the actual surround polygon in m2
exceptions: a documented project dimension replaces the default

rules.rule_name: The elevator surround is an area, and its polygon is built before it is measured
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §I, §J
required_geometry: the measurement basis and its source geometry
rules.calculation_method: construct the 2D cladding polygon of the three sides and take its UNION area. Never three-side linear perimeter x width, which counts the two top corners twice. ELEVATOR_SURROUND_AREA_M2 and ELEVATOR_SURROUND_EDGE_LM are kept separately and neither substitutes for the other
rules.notes: Urban Projects normally prefers this surround measured and priced by m2 rather than by linear metre

rules.rule_name: A typical station may stand for many only once equivalence is verified
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §K
rules.calculation_method: ONE VERIFIED TYPICAL STATION x VERIFIED COUNT, preserving every individual station id (ELV-01-GF, ELV-01-FF, ...). Nothing is multiplied until equivalence is established

rules.rule_name: The elevator threshold is marble, measured separately, with a fallback size
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §L, fallback confirmed in the 6E-A addendum §16
required_geometry: the front exposed edge where applicable
rules.calculation_method: ELEVATOR_THRESHOLD_MARBLE as its own object: width x depth in m2, and the exposed front edge in lm. ACTUAL DRAWING DIMENSIONS FIRST. Where none are available the Urban Projects fallback is 1.10 m x 0.50 m = 0.55 m2 — and where the door width IS established and only the depth is not, the width stays what the drawing says and only the 0.50 m depth is borrowed. A known dimension is never replaced by a default. It is never merged into the vertical door surround, and ELEVATOR_THRESHOLD_MARBLE_AREA n PORCELAIN_FLOOR_AREA = 0 m2 holds
rules.notes: the fallback is a DEFAULT and not mandatory geometry: a drawing, a detail or a project note replaces either dimension on its own

rules.rule_name: Stair tread marble is 30 mm thick
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 6E-A §1
required_geometry: the stair tread detail where the drawing gives one
rules.calculation_method: TREAD_MARBLE_THICKNESS = 0.030 m unless the drawing, specification or owner establishes another. It is the build-up subtracted from the step rise to give the VISIBLE riser (UP-STAIR-003)
exceptions: a drawn tread detail replaces it
rules.notes: a tread and a landing are not the same thickness: see UP-STAIR-007

rules.rule_name: Stair landing marble is 20 mm thick
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 6E-A §1
required_geometry: the landing detail where the drawing gives one
rules.calculation_method: LANDING_MARBLE_THICKNESS = 0.020 m unless the drawing, specification or owner establishes another. The 30 mm tread thickness is NOT used for a normal landing
exceptions: a drawn landing detail replaces it

rules.rule_name: Marble steps are commercially measured by linear metre of step width
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 6E-A §2, §3, §6
required_geometry: the width of each physical step
the cross-plan reconciliation that makes the steps unique
rules.calculation_method: STAIR_STEP_COMMERCIAL_LM = SUM(width of each UNIQUE physical step). The commercial step covers tread, riser and nosing together. It is NEVER derived from a tread area, and a step drawn on two plans is one step. The landing is measured in m2 and the skirting in lm, and neither is multiplied by the step basis
exceptions: a project or supplier that quotes on another basis records that basis on the project, not here
rules.notes: what a supplier charges for one of these metres belongs to a project rate card with its quotation and its date, never to this rule

rules.rule_name: نايم is the stair tread
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §C and 6E-A §18
rules.calculation_method: a term, not a quantity: نايم names the horizontal surface of a step. How it is measured is UP-STAIR-003 and UP-STAIR-008

rules.rule_name: قائم is the stair riser
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §C and 6E-A §18
rules.calculation_method: a term, not a quantity: قائم names the vertical face of a step. What of it is clad is the VISIBLE riser, UP-STAIR-003

rules.rule_name: استراحة is the stair landing
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 2026-09-17 §G and 6E-A §8, §18
rules.calculation_method: a term, not a quantity: استراحة names the piece a stair arrives at and turns on. Whether a given piece of floor IS one is decided on geometry, never on the word

rules.rule_name: وزرة or نعلة الدرج is the stair skirting
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 6E-A §9, §18
rules.calculation_method: a term, not a quantity: the skirting that follows the stair. Measured in lm, separately, and never inside the step basis or the landing area
rules.notes: وزرة and نعلة الدرج name the STAIR's skirting; توشيح names it too (UP-VOCAB-005). نعلة on its own is the ordinary room skirting, UP-CER-002 — the same word does different work with and without الدرج, and the two are not merged

rules.rule_name: A typical finished rise is a sanity range, never a measurement
rules.source: Owner rule addendum 6E-A §10
rules.calculation_method: a finished step rise commonly falls around 0.155-0.165 m. This is a DIAGNOSTIC SANITY RANGE and produces no quantity: a riser height comes from the floor-to-floor rise over a counted number of risers. A level is never assigned to a stair because the difference happens to fall in this range

rules.rule_name: Geometry and commercial pricing are separate
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: a physical quantity is measured from the drawing; a commercial quantity is how the work is bought. They are two fields, reported side by side, and neither is derived from the other

rules.rule_name: Four quantities, and they are never one number
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: MEASURED_NET is what the drawing gives; WASTE is a rule applied to it; PROCUREMENT is what is ordered; CONTRACTOR_COMMERCIAL is what is quoted and paid. Each is reported under its own name and no total spans them

rules.rule_name: Openings are deducted where applicable
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: the opening's own width and height
rules.calculation_method: doors, windows and other openings are deducted from the quantity they interrupt — a skirting run, a wall tile area, a waterproofing upturn. WHERE APPLICABLE is decided per rule and stated there, never assumed silently

rules.rule_name: A contractor rule never alters physical geometry
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: a commercial convention changes what is PAID FOR, not what is BUILT. No contractor-specific rule may move a wall, resize a room or change a measured area

rules.rule_name: Dry floor ceramic is measured in square metres
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: the room's released floor polygon in m2. A stair footprint, a marble threshold and any other finish's area are out of it

rules.rule_name: Normal dry skirting (نعلة) is measured in linear metres
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: the run of the room's finished wall base, in lm

rules.rule_name: Door openings are deducted from skirting
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: each door opening's width in the run
rules.calculation_method: SKIRTING_LM = wall base run - the width of every door opening in that run. A threshold is not skirting

rules.rule_name: A wet room with full wall ceramic receives no normal floor skirting
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: whether the room's wall ceramic is full height
rules.calculation_method: where the wall ceramic runs full height, the skirting quantity for that room is ZERO — the wall tile already reaches the floor. It is zero because the rule says so, not because nobody measured it, and the room is reported with the reason
exceptions: a wet room whose wall ceramic is NOT full height keeps its skirting

rules.rule_name: Wall ceramic is the eligible wall area less openings
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: NET_WALL_CERAMIC_M2 = gross eligible wall area - openings. The eligible area is the wall the drawing tiles, at the height the project establishes, and no universal height exists

rules.rule_name: A 45-degree ceramic edge is the exposed edge in lm
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: which edges of the tiled area are exposed
rules.calculation_method: the ACTUAL eligible exposed edge, in lm. Not the perimeter of the tiled area and not every corner of it: the edge that is actually exposed and actually mitred

rules.rule_name: A steel edge profile is a separate alternative to the 45-degree edge
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: measured in lm as its own item. It is an ALTERNATIVE to the 45-degree finish on the same edge: one edge takes one of them, and an edge counted in both is counted twice
exceptions: MITRED_EDGE_LM and STEEL_PROFILE_LM never cover the same edge

rules.rule_name: A floor drain (صفاية) is counted, not measured
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: a quantity in pieces. Its own area is not deducted from the floor unless the project says so

rules.rule_name: توشيح / تواشيح is the stair skirting
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: a term, not a quantity: the skirting that follows a stair. Measured in lm along its ACTUAL path, and never inside the step basis or the landing area
rules.notes: نعلة on its own is the ordinary room skirting (UP-CER-002); نعلة الدرج and وزرة and توشيح all name the stair's

rules.rule_name: A zigzag توشيح is measured along its zigzag
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: each step's going and rise along the skirting side
rules.calculation_method: the ACTUAL zigzag path in lm — the length that follows every step's nose and riser. Not the straight line from the bottom of the flight to the top, which is shorter than what is cut

rules.rule_name: A sloped توشيح is measured along its slope
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: the flight's plan run and its total rise
rules.calculation_method: the ACTUAL inclined path in lm — the rake of the flight, which is longer than its plan run

rules.rule_name: A railing follows the open edge and nothing else
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: which side of each flight is open
rules.calculation_method: RAILING_LM = the ACTUAL open-edge path of the stair. A side against a wall receives no railing, and a flight between two walls receives none at all
exceptions: a wall side takes a handrail only where the project says so, and that is a different item

rules.rule_name: Wet-room floor waterproofing is measured in m2
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: the wet room's floor area in m2, membrane under the finish

rules.rule_name: The waterproofing wall upturn is 0.15 m
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
rules.calculation_method: the membrane turns up the wall 0.15 m above the floor, all round. UPTURN_M2 = the run of the wet room's walls x 0.15, less the openings that interrupt it
exceptions: a project detail that states another upturn replaces it

rules.rule_name: The membrane continues through the doorway
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: the doorway's width and the depth it carries through
rules.calculation_method: the membrane does not stop at the door line: it continues through the doorway so the room can be flood tested. The doorway piece is part of the waterproofing area and is NOT deducted as an opening
exceptions: this is the one place where a door is not a deduction

rules.rule_name: A shower takes the same floor and upturn rule
rules.source: Urban Projects QS Rule Pack — Finishes V1, 2026-09-17
required_geometry: the shower's own floor area and wall run
rules.calculation_method: the shower's floor in m2 and the same 0.15 m upturn. A higher tanking to the shower walls is a separate item and a separate rule
